Good instinct, and the plumbing is actually halfway there already. Right now V/OI ratio isn't part of scoring at all -- the alert score is purely premium (0-6 pts) plus volume surprise (0-4 pts). V/OI gets *calculated* for display in the console output and email digests, and it's used as a post-hoc filter for social posting eligibility, but it has zero influence on whether an alert fires or how high it scores.

So mechanically, what you're describing would be a third component in `_calculate_flow_score()` in fm_analyzer.py. Something like: if OI < 1000 and volume/OI > some threshold (say 5x? 10x?), add bonus points. That's straightforward to implement.

The thing I'd want to be careful about: low OI contracts are also where you get the noisiest data. A contract with 12 OI that suddenly prints 200 volume could be genuine new positioning, or it could be a market maker adjusting a hedge, or just someone rolling out of a position that was opened ages ago. The signal-to-noise ratio gets worse as OI shrinks. So I think the threshold and the bonus magnitude matter a lot here -- you'd want it to boost genuinely interesting activity without promoting noise into the alert stream.

TA, what's your read on this from the trading side? Is there a V/OI ratio or OI floor where you'd say 'yeah, that's almost certainly new money coming in' versus 'could be anything'?
